title: Metromoney: One Card for the Metro, Buses, Minibuses and Cable Cars
excerpt: Tbilisi runs on one municipal operator and one anonymous card: the Metromoney buys a 90-minute window across the two metro lines, the blue buses, the numbered minibuses and the Bagebi–University ropeway, with bank cards accepted on everything. Rike–Narikala and Turtle Lake charge their own fares, the funicular wants a different card altogether, Rustaveli Avenue is closed until December 2026, and the airport is bus 337 or the official rank — never the man in the terminal.
bodyHtml:
One company, one card

Almost everything municipal in Tbilisi belongs to the Tbilisi Transport Company (TTC), wholly owned by City Hall: the metro since 1966, the city buses since 2009, the Rike–Narikala cable car since 2012, the parking since 2018. Head office Station Square No. 2; hotline 032 293 44 44. The card is the Metromoney: anonymous, no ID needed, valid on the metro, the buses, the city minibuses and three cable cars. Buy it at any metro station payment office (the salaro window) or at the Rike–Narikala ticket offices; TTC also lists Bank of Georgia express branches. Top up at any metro station, at both Rike–Narikala stations, and at Bank of Georgia express-pay machines (the orange-and-white boxes, cash) and service centres. Whether TBC pay boxes load it too is ⚠ VERIFY: TTC's own page names only Bank of Georgia. The balance shows on the metro gate as you pass and on the bus ticket.

The receipt trap. TTC restores a lost or damaged Metromoney only against the receipt printed when you bought it — no receipt, no transfer of balance, and the card's refund within a month needs it too. Photograph it. The 'problematic card' desks are inside Avlabari and Medical University stations.

The 90-minute rule

TTC's standard tariff is a time window, not a ride: one tap buys 90 minutes of unlimited travel across the metro, the buses, the minibuses and the Bagebi–University ropeway — metro, bus, metro again on a single fare. Day, week, month and longer passes exist, but only on a personalised subscription card from a metro payment office. TTC's page extends the package to 'different bank cards', so a contactless Visa, Mastercard or phone boards everything; recent guides report a higher per-tap charge for foreign cards and disagree on whether they earn the transfers — ⚠ VERIFY with your own card, then buy a Metromoney at the first window you pass. Two things definitely get no window: cash (still taken on some minibuses) and payment through the mobile app.

The metro: two lines, one interchange

Line 1, the Akhmeteli–Varketili line, runs 16 stations from Akhmetelis Teatri in the north to Varketili in the south-east; Line 2, the Saburtalo line, runs seven from Station Square out to State University (opened 2017). Station Square (Sadguris Moedani), under the central railway station, is the only interchange. Trains run from a little before 06:00 until about midnight — ⚠ VERIFY the last train at your station; times vary. New CRRC trains ordered in 2025 are due from 2026.

Buses and minibuses

Route numbers are three digits: the 3xx (and 2xx) routes are TTC's full-size buses — blue MAN and green Isuzu, with 200 gas-powered 18-metre MANs entering service from 27 September 2025 — and the 4xx/5xx routes are minibuses run by the separate Tbilisi Minibus company (tm.ge). The old yellow marshrutkas were withdrawn in 2021–22 and replaced by blue-grey minibuses on fixed numbered routes; they still stop on request and still show the destination in Georgian. Metromoney and bank cards work on both. Rustaveli Avenue is closed to all traffic from 23 July to the end of November 2026 for rebuilding, between Tamar Chovelidze Street and Freedom Square: some twenty bus routes, 337 among them, are diverted via Heroes' Square and the embankment, and several minibuses no longer reach Rustaveli metro.

Live tracking

TTC's own app is Tbilisi Transport Company (iOS and Android, linked from ttc.com.ge): planner, live arrivals by stop, offline timetables, with the same data on the web at transit.ttc.com.ge. The 'Tbilisi Bus' app in the stores is third-party; Google Maps carries the live feed too.

Cable cars and the funicular

Rike–Narikala (2012), Rike Park to the fortress, is TTC's, charges its own single fare and takes Metromoney only — its windows sell the card. Hours are seasonal and TTC publishes none: ⚠ VERIFY at the lower station. Turtle Lake (Kus Tba), from 76 Chavchavadze Avenue beside Vake Park, reopened in 2016 with bike hooks and its own low fare; TTC took it out of service for maintenance on 23 December 2025 with no end date — ⚠ VERIFY it is running. The Bagebi–University ropeway, from the university's Maghlivi building across the Vere valley, is municipal transport inside the 90-minute window. The Mtatsminda funicular, from Daniel Chonkadze Street up to the park, is the park's, not TTC's: Metromoney is not valid; buy the park's own card at either station.

The airport

The airport's own transport pages list two things: bus 337 — stop in front of Arrivals, timetable 06:59 to 22:59, via Kakheti Highway, Avlabari and Freedom Square to Station Square, roughly every 15–20 minutes, Metromoney or bank card, diverted off Rustaveli until December — and the taxi rank. The railway station 70 metres from the terminal is no longer listed: guides updated in August 2026 say no trains are running, with a resumption 'later this year' — ⚠ VERIFY on gr.com.ge before planning around it.

The airport taxi trap. The official rank is at the kerb outside Arrivals, 24 hours, on the meter (tbstaxi.ge, +995 550 506040). Anyone who approaches you inside the terminal is not it — the reported fares are several times the app price. Order a Bolt instead; the terminal Wi-Fi is unreliable for apps, so use your own data.

Taxis in town

Bolt is the default — Estonian, card-in-app, Economy to XL plus an Electric option. Yandex Go is often cheaper but is Russian-owned: in September 2024 Georgia's Personal Data Protection Service fined its local operator for sending users' and drivers' IP addresses to servers in Russia, and many Georgians boycott it on principle. Choose knowingly. Maxim is the third app. Sit in the back.

Leaving town

Three stations, by direction. Didube (Okriba), 153 Tsereteli Avenue at Didube metro: everything north and west — Mtskheta, Gudauri, Kazbegi, Gori, Borjomi, Kutaisi, Batumi. Navtlughi beside Samgori metro: Kakheti — Sighnaghi, Telavi. Ortachala, the Central Bus Station at 5 Dimitri Gulia Street, has no metro and now mostly handles international coaches (Yerevan, Baku, Turkey), ticketed on tkt.ge. A ban on minibuses over 150 km and between the big cities was announced for 1 June 2025; guides report it deferred to 2027 — ⚠ VERIFY, but the vans are running. Trains leave Tbilisi Central above Station Square: Stadler double-deckers to Batumi via Kutaisi Airport, sold out days ahead in summer — book on gr.com.ge or tkt.ge — the daily Baku train, back since 26 May 2026, and Yerevan.

On foot and behind the wheel

The old town, Sololaki and Mtatsminda are staircases as much as streets, and the metro leaves you at the bottom of them; a Bolt up and a walk down is the local pattern. Driving is fast and improvised, and central parking is TTC's zonal-hour system, paid through the Tbilisi Parking app. Most newcomers never buy a car.
